ety.text: Inherited from Old Hindi आथना (āthanā), from Prakrit 𑀅𑀢𑁆𑀣𑀺 (atthi), from Sanskrit अस्ति (asti).

s.g: to behave in an affected style with airs
to act with contrived grace, to act fancily

ety.text: A verbalization of Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀇𑀢𑁆𑀢𑀭 (ittara) (from Sanskrit इत्वर (itvará, “walking, strutting”)) with -आ- (-ā-) + -ना (-nā, verbal suffix).

s.g: the Indian birthwort (Aristolochia indica), said to be an antidote to snake poison.
to throw out, pour off; to drain

ety.text: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit *𑀉𑀮𑁆𑀮𑀺𑀘𑁆𑀘𑀤𑀺 (*ulliccadi) (compare 𑀉𑀮𑁆𑀮𑀺𑀁𑀘𑀤𑀺 (ulliṃcadi, “empties”)), from Sanskrit उद्रिच्यते (udricyate, “is prominent”). All later forms of the Sanskrit verb have basic meaning of uncompounded रिच् (ric, “to leave, empty, pour”), e.g. Pali uddekanika (“spouting”).
Borrowed from Sanskrit एकवचन (ekavacana). Analyzable as एक (ek, “one, single”) + वचन (vacan, “grammatical number”).

ety.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian دیر (dēr), from Old Persian 𐎭𐎼𐎥 (darga), from Proto-Iranian *dr̥Hgáh (compare Avestan 𐬛𐬀𐬭𐬆𐬔𐬀 (dar^əga, “long”)), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *dr̥Hgʰás (compare Sanskrit दीर्घ (dīrghá)), from Proto-Indo-European *dl̥h₁gʰós (compare Latin longus, Old Church Slavonic дльгъ (dlĭgŭ)). Doublet of दीह (dīh) and दीर्घ (dīrgh).

Borrowed from Classical Persian فَنّ (fann) or directly from Arabic فَنّ (fann), from Classical Persian پَنْد (pand). Attested as Old Hindi फनी (phanī), फंनी (phaṃnī). Cognate with Punjabi ਫ਼ਨ (fan).
